content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: NIT Rourkela has 2 JRF vacancies in total, one in each project listed below. The notice states that a Project Associate (PA) will only be considered in case a JRF is not found suitable.

rows.project_title: PDC hybrids for sodium ion battery anodes

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The essential qualification for JRF is a Post Graduate degree in basic science OR a Graduate / Post Graduate Degree in a Professional Course, selected through one of the following: National Eligibility Tests: CSIR-UGC NET including Lectureship (Assistant Professorship), and GATE. A national eligibility examination conducted by Central Government departments and their agencies and institutions such as DBT, DST, DAE, DOS, DRDO, MoE, ICAR, ICMR, IIT, IISc, IISER, NISER, etc. Desirable qualifications, project-wise: Project E2.4: BE/B.Tech/M.Sc. (with GATE) with a CGPA of 7.0 or 65% marks, OR M.Tech in Ceramic Engg. / Metallurgical and Materials Engg. / Chemical Engg. / Mechanical Engg. / Biomedical Engg. / Nanotechnology / Biotechnology, OR MSc (with GATE) in Physics / Chemistry / Materials Science / Nano Science with at least 6.5 CGPA or 60% marks. Project A2.1: Master's Degree (M.Sc./Integrated M.Sc.) in Chemistry, preferably with a specialization in Organic Chemistry, with 65% marks or a CGPA of 6.5/10. A 5% relaxation in minimum qualifying marks applies to SC/ST/OBC (Non-Creamy Layer)/PwD candidates and women candidates. Project A2.1 also states that candidates must have secured First Class in Class 10, Class 12, B.Sc. and M.Sc. and qualified GATE/NET with score or rank. Candidates with a Master's degree in Chemistry who have qualified in national-level entrance examinations such as JEE or the Joint Admission Test for Master (JAM) are also eligible to apply. Candidates appearing for their final examination are also eligible to apply, but the qualifying degree result must be submitted by 31 December 2026. The period of experience, wherever prescribed, is counted after the date of acquiring the minimum prescribed educational qualification. The Project Associate – I (PA) qualification is a four years Bachelor's Degree in Natural or Agriculture Science, or a Master's Degree in Natural or Agriculture Sciences, or BVSc, or B. Pharm, or a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Technology or Medicine from a recognized University or equivalent. Age limit: the notice says "As per ANRF norms". Its age guideline says the upper age limit is relaxed for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, PwD and female applicants, with a separate figure for OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates. The upper age limit is reckoned as on the last date of receipt of applications. Candidates should check the official notice for the exact figures.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Engagement is purely on a temporary / contractual basis and co-terminus with the completion of the project. After joining, shared accommodation is provided in the hostel as per institute policy. Selected candidates must register for the Ph.D. programme. The date of joining is on or before 31 December 2026.

rows.post: PA (considered only if JRF is not found suitable)

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NIT Rourkela Junior Research Fellow (JRF)
content_sections.text: The notice states that no hard copies of applications are required to be sent to the Institute. Documents named in the notice: Complete filled and signed application Educational qualification documents with percentage of marks and division (marksheets and/or certificates) Research papers, if any Work experience certificate, if any

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Candidates are shortlisted based on merit and need of the project. Possession of the minimum qualification alone does not guarantee an invitation to the interview, and NIT Rourkela reserves the right to fix higher criteria for shortlisting. Only shortlisted candidates are informed. The activity schedule lists a test / interview in person at NIT Rourkela on 2 December 2026, with the result of scrutiny intimated by email on 30 November 2026 and selection intimated by email on 5 December 2026. Selection and joining will be cancelled in case of any suppression of information or document submitted.

faq.question: Q1. How many JRF vacancies are there at NIT Rourkela?
faq.answer: There are 2 Junior Research Fellow vacancies, one in project E2.4 (PDC hybrids for sodium ion battery anodes) and one in project A2.1 (Organic Synthesis).

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the NIT Rourkela JRF posts?
faq.answer: The last date of submission of application by email is 27 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for NIT Rourkela JRF?
faq.answer: A Post Graduate degree in basic science, or a Graduate / Post Graduate Degree in a Professional Course, selected through CSIR-UGC NET, GATE or a national eligibility examination of Central Government departments and agencies.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the NIT Rourkela JRF posts?
faq.answer: The notice says the age limit is as per ANRF norms. The upper age limit is reckoned as on the last date of receipt of applications, with relaxation for SC, ST, PwD, female and OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates.

faq.question: Q5. What is the pay of a JRF at NIT Rourkela?
faq.answer: The post details print ₹27,000 per month for years 1 and 2 and ₹42,000 per month from year 3 onwards till completion of the project.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the NIT Rourkela JRF posts?
faq.answer: Send the filled and signed application with qualification documents as a single PDF to [email protected], copying the relevant investigator, with the Advertisement No. in the subject line. Hard copies are not required.

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected for the NIT Rourkela JRF posts?
faq.answer: Candidates are shortlisted based on merit and need of the project, and shortlisted candidates attend a test / interview in person at NIT Rourkela on 2 December 2026.

faq.question: Q8. Is the NIT Rourkela JRF job permanent?
faq.answer: No, the engagement is purely on a temporary / contractual basis and co-terminus with the completion of the project.

faq.question: Q9. Can final-year students apply for the NIT Rourkela JRF posts?
faq.answer: Yes, candidates appearing for their final examination can apply, but the qualifying degree result must be submitted by 31 December 2026.

faq.question: Q10. Do selected JRFs have to register for a Ph.D.?
faq.answer: Yes, the notice states that selected candidates are required to register for the Ph.D. programme.
